subject: App integration: safety-net retry/timeouts + SDK hints
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@quicksprint.com>, integration@quicksprint.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: App integration: safety-net retry/timeouts + SDK hints

Alex / QuickSprint team —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. I pulled together a short set of practical recommendations to make the SDK integration resilient during your migration from the existing endpoint to the new /v2 generation endpoints. No surprises — these are conservative patterns we push for early-stage cutovers to avoid traffic storms and to make rollbacks predictable.

High-level asks
- Please confirm sandbox API key (integration@quicksprint.com has a test key?) and the expected cutover date for traffic (even a rough week is fine).
- Share any hard rate limits on your side (requests/sec per token or per-account) so we can tune the client-side throttles.

Recommended safety-net patterns (summary)
1) Client-side rate limit guard
   - Track X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers; when remaining < 5, enter a 1s+ jittered pause before retrying.
2) Exponential backoff with capped concurrency
   - Retry policy: up to 5 retries for 429/503. Backoff = base * (2^attempt) * (1 + jitter). Base = 200ms. Max backoff = 10s.
3) Short per-request timeouts + streaming keepalive
   - SDK default request timeout: 10s for single-shot generate, 30s for streaming with incremental reads.
4) Prefix caching for repeat prompts
   - Cache prefixes for 60s when identical session/metadata to avoid repeated identical token cost spikes.

Minimal example snippets (attach full bundle)
- curl (simple):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST-KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"gpt-3-mini","prompt":"Summarize...","max_tokens":150}' --max-time 10

- Node (axios) retry skeleton:
  const axios = require('axios');
  async function callGenerate(payload) {
    const maxRetries = 5;
    for (let i=0;i<=maxRetries;i++) {
      try {
        const resp = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate', payload, {
          headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          timeout: 10000
        });
        return resp.data;
      } catch (err) {
        const status = err.response && err.response.status;
        if (i === maxRetries || (status && status < 500 && status !== 429)) throw err;
        const backoff = Math.min(10000, 200 * Math.pow(2, i) * (1 + Math.random()*0.3));
        await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoff));
      }
    }
  }

Attachments: retry-snippets.zip (small examples: axios/node/python + telemetry template)

I'll follow up with a proposed canary rollout checklist and an ops Slack channel invite. If you want a one-hour walkthrough tomorrow, propose a time and I can invite Vivek to cover the canary/SGA side.

—Mina

Subject: Re: App integration: safety-net retry/timeouts + SDK hints

Thanks Mina — really helpful. A couple quick items from our side:
- We currently enforce a per-tenant rate limit of 120 reqs/min with bursts allowed up to 200 for short periods. We do return X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.
- For streaming calls we set a socket-level idle timeout at 45s.

Question: for 429s do you recommend immediate retry with backoff (as above) or should we bias to queueing at the client gateway and drain? We have some local gateways that could buffer short bursts.

Also: can you confirm whether /v2 will return a distinct header for model-variant fallback events? We want to tag logs when a fallback to a smaller quantized variant happens.

Appreciate the snippets — we'll unzip and try them out.

—Alex
Principal PM, QuickSprint
alex.cheng@quicksprint.com

Alex — great, that's helpful context. Two short notes addressing your points: 

1) Queueing vs immediate retry
- If you control a client gateway that can do short-term in-memory queueing (<= 10s) and shed carefully on overflow, that is preferable for burst smoothing. It reduces request churn hitting the origin and helps preserve per-tenant fairness.
- For user-facing interactive flows prefer fast retries with exponential backoff and a small client-side queue (e.g., 50 concurrent queue slots) so perceived latency stays low.

2) Model-variant fallbacks
- /v2 responses include: X-Model-Variant and X-Fallback-Triggered headers when automatic fallback occurs. We recommend emitting a structured log event when X-Fallback-Triggered=true for later quality/regression analysis.

Concrete canary plan (high level)
- Phase 0 (pre-cutover): smoke tests from your staging IPs; success criteria = 95% requests < 200ms P95 and no 5xx spike.
- Phase 1 (1% traffic): enable prefix caching and client concurrency cap = 10. Monitor rate-limit headers and model-quality metrics.
- Phase 2 (10%): increase concurrency cap to 50, enable limited burst allowance on the client gateway.
- Phase 3: full cutover with rollback window and a feature flag to pin to older endpoint if quality regressions exceed threshold.

Telemetry/alerts to wire up
- Emit: request_id, model_variant, fallback_triggered, latency_p95, tokens_generated, client_region, billing_account_id.
- Alert on: sustained 429 rate > 1% over 10m, model-fallback > 0.5% over 15m, P95 latency regression > 30% vs baseline.

I'll attach the telemetry template; it's under integration-telemetry-template.md in the zip. Monica, Vivek — tagging you for the rollout scheduling and SGA review.

—Mina
